messages.author: 9a039f550ead796f
messages.subject: write.csv connection issues shiny server
parts:
Hi all,

I have recently deployed my first shiny app on my shiny server rather than run locally. It all works very well, reading in some data, manipulating, but fails to write.csv the data back to the server (/srv/shiny-server/MyApp/data), even though it reads from the same location.

If this is a permissions problem, can anyone give detailed advice on how to approach? Newbie in the linux/server space!

Very much appreciated

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: write.csv connection issues shiny server
parts:
Hi,

This is most likely a permission issue. By default the R process for your application runs as user "shiny" (if you haven't changed this user in your configuration file). This user has read permission to the /srv/shiny-server directory but not write permission. You can open up permissions on this folder to allow write by all users, or you could make this directory (and its children) to be owned by "shiny" user. You should consider the security of your system as far as access to directories and files, and make the judgement on how to allow "write" to these directories.

The other option is to use "user_dirs" hosting model. Admin Guide has details on how to setup your system for this hosting model, and an example of configuration file for this is located here. With this model you will copy your applications to a "ShinyApps" directory in your home directory, where you have write permissions to them. And you can configure it such that R process runs as you (not the "shiny" user). 

Let us know if you need more help with setting up your Shiny Server. You can also send me private email if you prefer.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: write.csv connection issues shiny server
parts: To add to what Fereshteh said, to change permissions you want to use the "chmod" command and to change owners you want to use "chown". Google should turn up lots of articles about each command. I think changing the ownership rather than permissions is probably the better approach in this case. Or better yet, have a dedicated subdirectory of your app where you write data, and only chown that subdirectory.

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: write.csv connection issues shiny server
parts:
can you send ls -l of the /srv/shiny-server/Elections/USA2016/shiny/Temp directory?

Might be that files in there still don't have correct ownership/permissions.

if so, to fix, try
 
chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/Elections/USA2016/shiny/Temp/


-R makes it recursive which will change the ownership for all files in Temp, assumign Temp is where you're writing.


For good measure, also try

chmod -R 755 /srv/shiny-server/Elections/USA2016/shiny/Temp/


755 will make the files writable



report back
